nodes.text: For dispute DSP-2026-90122, the cardholder's non-receipt account is corroborated by a delivery-address mismatch: the customer lived at ADR-C12B-HOME (610 Grove Lane, unit 3C) during the purchase, while ParcelPath shipment SHP-C12B (PP-C12B-8841) was marked delivered by a door photo with no signer to ADR-C12B-WRONG (601 Grove Lane, unit 3C). No refund is linked, and the merchant evidence request ERQ-C12B passed its 2026-10-19 deadline without a response.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.text: For DSP-2026-90122 / TXN-C12B, the order for two bedside lamps ($284.20) was placed 2026-10-02 and linked to shipment SHP-C12B (ParcelPath tracking PP-C12B-8841) shipped 2026-10-04. The shipment's proof of delivery is a door photo at 601 Grove Lane, unit 3C (ADR-C12B-WRONG), while the cardholder's recorded residence is 610 Grove Lane, unit 3C (ADR-C12B-HOME); therefore the available fulfillment evidence supports delivery to the wrong address, not normal delivery to the intended location. No carrier-event nodes or evidence establish acceptance, route progression, attempted delivery, exception, or reroute; merchant evidence was requested and marked no_response.

TXN-C12-01 has no FROM_IP edge; its order also has no FROM_IP edge. Compared with TXN-C12-02 through TXN-C12-04, all four are separate primary accounts/cards (CRD-C12-01 through CRD-C12-04), have no transaction token or card-tokenization evidence, no customer LOGGED_IN_FROM or account-event authentication evidence, and use the same shared device DEV-C12-SHARED. The graph therefore establishes shared household infrastructure, not customer-specific IP, authentication, token, or account evidence of unauthorized use for TXN-C12-01.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: A repeated device shared by multiple customers at a common address, even with sequential purchases at the same merchant and matching non-receipt disputes, is a shared-infrastructure review signal—not proof of unauthorized use or coordinated fraud. Do not infer an unauthorized actor without customer-specific evidence such as source IP, authentication/login records, tokenization, account-compromise events, or other direct linkage; legitimate household use remains an alternative explanation.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: When a recorded delivery address exactly matches the customer's active residence, a door-photo/resident POD is positive corroboration of delivery to the intended address. If the POD lacks a named signer, signature image, delivery timestamp, or geolocation, it does not independently prove personal receipt; record those limitations as evidence gaps rather than treating them as proof of non-receipt or misdelivery.
